name: Shared Action Economy — Design Decisions
scope: One native action economy used by all combatants regardless of Standard or Complex model, character options, or selected initiative mode.

approvedDecisions.unifiedSystem: Use one Dorks & Dice action economy for 3.x/PF1e and 5.x concepts rather than parallel edition-specific turns.
approvedDecisions.movement: Independent 5.x-style movement allowance may be split around permitted activities, including between attacks when their procedures permit it.
approvedDecisions.fullTurnConstraints: Explicitly authorized full-turn/full-round restrictions constrain ordinary movement and action usage when their own rules require them; they are not automatically erased by flexible movement.

nativeTerminology.rationale: Preserve the established D&D 5.x term for familiarity.
doesNotImply: Immediate Actions are automatically equivalent to Reactions or consume the same resource.
Every imported Swift Action feature overrides its own prerequisites, targets, resource costs, or other explicit restrictions.
Any actor may perform a Bonus Action without an applicable grant or rule.

approvedDecisions.initiative: Standard initiative and optional Block Initiative use the same per-combatant action-economy rules; Block Initiative does not pool allied action budgets.

bonusActionSwiftUnification.unifiedBudget: One Bonus Action opportunity per combatant turn under the ordinary baseline. A qualifying Swift Action or Bonus Action spends that same opportunity; possessing options from both sources does not grant an additional action.
bonusActionSwiftUnification.eligibility: A feature, spell, item, or applicable rule must explicitly authorize the activity. Multiple authorized choices compete for the same allowance.
bonusActionSwiftUnification.timing: The ordinary allowance is used on the actor's turn unless a more specific approved rule establishes a valid exception; it does not grant out-of-turn activation.
bonusActionSwiftUnification.preservation: Preserve individual source-derived ability prerequisites, casting components, resource costs, effect limits, and explicitly authorized exceptions during conversion. Consolidating action categories does not erase those properties.
bonusActionSwiftUnification.immediateActionBoundary: 3.x Immediate Action timing and its historical use of a current or upcoming Swift Action are NOT automatically imported as native Bonus Action/Reaction costs; establish a separate explicit mapping before implementing those interactions.
bonusActionSwiftUnification.initiative: The allowance belongs to each combatant under either standard initiative or optional Block Initiative, not a shared allied block pool.

pendingDecisions: Whether ordinary Reactions and Bonus Actions share an allowance, including a strict shared pool versus borrowing the next turn's Bonus Action.
Feature-specific exceptions to the ordinary one-Bonus-Action-per-turn allowance and timing, if justified by a distinct grant.
Precise conversion of atypical 3.x/PF1e Swift Action timing restrictions, and how swift casting interacts with native spellcasting limitations.
Whether and how Immediate Actions interact with Reactions and the current or upcoming Bonus Action budget; this is a separate design decision.
Native opportunity attack triggers, eligible reactive actions and reaction refresh.
Nonmovement move-equivalent action conversion, Action substitution and full-turn constraints.
Free activity/object interaction limits, interruption ordering, durations and Block Initiative timing details.
implementationBoundary: The two action-budget policies have experimental, opt-in resource-only runtime evaluation. Neither policy is an approved native action-economy rule, automatically activated, integrated with combat effects, or a source-conversion default.

openDesignInvestigation.status: owner-proposed; undecided; not an approved gameplay rule
openDesignInvestigation.ownerHypothesis: A shared Bonus Action and Reaction resource could make unused Bonus Action capacity feel like reactive insurance, reducing the need to assign routine Bonus Actions to all classes.
openDesignInvestigation.qualification: In 5.x a character without an eligible Bonus Action already has a Reaction allowance. Coupling would primarily increase the cost of Bonus Actions for other characters; it grants no new Reaction.

candidates.rule: Bonus Action and Reaction have separate allowances, as in 5.x.
candidates.risk: Some characters have no Bonus Action choice; could address separately through class design.

candidates.rule: Using either Bonus Action or Reaction spends the same allowance until the next refresh.
candidates.risk: Using a Bonus Action could disable opportunity attacks, defense and cooperative Reactions before the next turn.

candidates.rule: One shared Bonus Action/Reaction allowance refreshes at the end of each combatant's own turn. An available allowance can pay for a qualifying Bonus Action on the combatant's turn or a qualifying Reaction when its trigger occurs. An out-of-turn Reaction spends the allowance until the end of the combatant's next turn, thereby displacing their next Bonus Action without recording a separate debt. Spending a Bonus Action during a turn does not block Reactions after that turn ends, because the allowance refreshes at turn end.
candidates.risk: This is simple to track, but can still change 5.x conversion balance, penalize frequent Bonus Action users, and prevent multiple uses of this shared resource between refreshes. Reaction trigger eligibility, initial resource state, explicit extra grants, end-of-turn order, and Block Initiative semantics still need specification.
candidates.label: One shared resource, end-of-turn refresh (future-borrowing behavior)

candidates.rule: Ordinary budgets are separate, but an explicitly identified high-impact Reaction can consume the upcoming Bonus Action.
candidates.risk: Mechanics and source conversions must distinguish which abilities bear additional costs.

openDesignInvestigation.alternative: Future class redesign could offer worthwhile eligible Bonus Action options; Warlock remains the only playable class experiment and no general class-design decision has been approved.
keyTests: Character with no eligible Bonus Action, whether a Reaction trigger appears or not
Character uses Bonus Action on own turn and an enemy then provokes an opportunity attack
Dual-wielding, Rogue Cunning Action and defensive spell interactions
Out-of-turn Reaction followed by a desired Bonus Action on the next turn
On-turn Reaction, Ready, interruption and refresh timing
Standard versus Block Initiative per-actor timing and mixed Standard/Complex Combatants
Separate treatment of imported 3.x Immediate Actions and ordinary opportunity attacks
decisionNeeded: Whether any universal coupling is desirable
Strict shared allowance versus borrowing next turn versus independent baseline
Whether ordinary opportunity attacks and all other Reactions participate
Exact budget refresh, on-turn reactions, first-turn behavior and special grants
Interaction with future class redesign and mixed-complexity players
openDesignInvestigation.implementationBoundary: Comparison only; preserves prior approved one-Bonus-Action-per-turn category and changes no runtime action economy.

ownerComparativeAssessment.status: comparative preference only; no mechanics approved
ownerComparativeAssessment.reason: The 3.x-style model borrows from the next turn rather than denying a Reaction because of a Bonus Action already spent on the preceding turn. It can preserve the opportunity to react and make the subsequent tradeoff more meaningful.
ownerComparativeAssessment.boundary: Owner prefers future borrowing to the earlier strict shared-resource proposal, but has NOT selected future borrowing as the native rule. Independent budgets, selective coupling, the scope of affected Reactions, and all timing/refresh details remain open.

reactionOpportunityCostObservation.status: owner observation and comparative analysis; NOT an approved mechanics change
reactionOpportunityCostObservation.insight: In 5.x, offensive opportunity attacks and defensive reactive abilities both consume the same Reaction. A combatant must choose whether to use that out-of-turn allowance to attack or to preserve it for defense. This offers a meaningful reactive choice without drawing on Bonus Action availability.
reactionOpportunityCostObservation.historicalDistinction: In the ordinary 3.5e/PF1e models, attacks of opportunity have an allowance distinct from Swift/Immediate Actions. Immediate Actions borrow the next Swift Action when used out of turn; ordinary attacks of opportunity do not automatically make that exchange.
reactionOpportunityCostObservation.implication: If the 5.x shared offensive/defensive Reaction remains native, making every Reaction also borrow the next Bonus Action would add a second cost to an already competing resource, not merely reproduce the original 3.x choice. Test the extra cost before endorsing universal borrowing.
doesNotDecide: Whether the native Reaction allowance and default opportunity attack costs follow 5.x precisely
Whether future borrowing should apply to any or all native Reactions
Whether some defensive/offensive reactions justify explicit extra costs
Class-redesign policy for Bonus Action choices or any refresh timing

ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.status: owner concern and option exploration; NOT approval to enable or implement a variant
ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.expectedPrimaryUse: Owner expects many adopters to convert 5.x characters, creatures, abilities, and encounters into Dorks & Dice. This is an expectation to test, not verified usage statistics.
ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.desiredGameplayValue: Future borrowing makes reacting a forward-looking opportunity-cost decision and may reward planning, positioning, and deliberate ability use; strict shared-pool coupling is less attractive to the owner.
ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.obstacle: An optional universal future-borrowing rule may change action costs and effective power across imported 5.x features that assumed independent Bonus Action and Reaction allowances. The rule could also create a substantial unfamiliarity barrier for players accustomed to 5.x.
asymmetricConsequences: A combatant with a frequently useful Bonus Action loses more on future borrowing than a combatant with no useful Bonus Action.
Imported defensive Reactions, opportunity attacks, and cooperative Reaction contributions can become less attractive or unexpectedly expensive.
Converted enemy statblocks and mixed-complexity parties may also experience behavior changes; source conversion cannot guarantee original encounter balance under a different action economy.
A campaign-wide optional action economy could require a second supported balance/acceptance matrix for converted content, rather than becoming safe just by being optional.
ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.ownerIntent: Interested in retaining the tactical trade-off as an optional rule if viable, but currently considers the balance and onboarding implications serious enough that adopting it as an ordinary or supported optional rule may be unreasonable.
ownerConversionAndAccessibilityConcerns.architectureBoundary: A change to shared action budgets is an encounter/campaign rule, not an individual player's independent rules mode; the established single coherent encounter applies regardless of Standard/Complex Combatant model.

openAlternatives.description: Retain independent 5.x-like Bonus Action/Reaction costs as the ordinary native baseline; assess whether any variant is feasible separately.
If design and playtests eventually justify it, offer explicit opt-in at campaign/encounter scope with visible compatibility and balancing warnings, not automatic activation for converted 5.x content.
Consider explicitly granted native abilities that incur a future Bonus Action cost without making every standard 5.x Reaction or imported feature pay that cost.
Investigate positioning, telegraphed behaviors, Ready-like commitments, defenses and advanced maneuvers as sources of planning decisions without altering all imported reaction costs.

decisionsNotMade: No global or variant future-borrowing rule approved
No 5.x compatibility mode or campaign setting approved
No feature-specific resource borrowing grant approved
No native default Reaction budget or refresh contract approved
acceptanceQuestions: Does the variant meaningfully improve ordinary encounter decisions rather than merely make reactions rarer?
What existing 5.x Bonus Action/Reaction-heavy builds or monster features become weaker or stronger, and is this acceptable?
Do converted 5.x encounters remain playable without manual rebalancing?
Can first-time 5.x players understand and consciously opt into a different cost model?
Can simpler and advanced players still participate in one coherent encounter?
Are the development, testing and support costs justified compared with targeted tactical features?

ownerTimingSimplification.status: owner clarification of candidate mechanics; not approval
ownerTimingSimplification.suggestedRule: A combatant has one shared allowance for an eligible Bonus Action or Reaction. The allowance refreshes at the end of that combatant's turn.
ownerTimingSimplification.realization: The future-turn cost follows directly from the refresh timing. There is no need for a 'borrowed next turn' ledger or separate future debt.
sequence: Combatant enters their own turn with the allowance available, provided they have not reacted since their previous end-of-turn refresh.
If the combatant spends the allowance on an eligible Bonus Action during their turn, it refreshes when their turn ends.
If the combatant then uses a qualifying Reaction before their next turn, the allowance remains spent at the start of the next turn.
They cannot spend that allowance on a Bonus Action during the next turn; it refreshes again when that turn ends.
ownerTimingSimplification.compatibilityWarning: This simplifies state tracking but does not resolve differences in effective 5.x class power, imported monster reactions, cooperative actions, or player familiarity.
stillOpen: Whether to adopt the shared end-of-turn-refresh allowance at all, even as an optional campaign rule
Whether all reactions or only a defined subset consume it
Start-of-encounter availability and turn-end ordering for reactions or triggers occurring at the boundary
Extra/replaced actions, reactions during one's own turn, and Block Initiative per-combatant turn boundaries
Compatibility and balancing tests for 5.x converted content

policies.label: Independent 5.x-style budgets
policies.refresh: Both Bonus Action and Reaction allowances refresh at the start of each individual combatant's turn.
policies.cost: A Bonus Action spends only the Bonus Action allowance. A Reaction spends only the Reaction allowance.

policies.label: Single shared allowance, end-of-turn refresh
policies.refresh: The combined Bonus Action/Reaction allowance refreshes at the end of each individual combatant's turn.
policies.cost: Either eligible Bonus Action or Reaction spends the combined allowance. Out-of-turn Reaction use can leave the next turn without an available Bonus Action.

playtestPrototype.use: Explicitly opt into one policy for an entire playtest encounter; persist resource snapshots per combatant in the consumer. No policy is implicitly selected or activated for conversion.
constraints: No changes to action kinds, named ability eligibility, legal triggers, costs other than action-resource accounting, or effects.
Applies equally to Standard and Complex Combatants and to either initiative mode.
Authorization of activities and reaction triggers remains the responsibility of the encounter consumer; a budget showing available is not permission to act.
This prototype cannot validate that the caller kept one policy for all combatants or that caller-submitted state is authentic; encounter tooling must enforce those boundaries.
No authoritative game-rule selection, state persistence, UI integration, source conversion, or release is implied.
playtestPrototype.review: See docs/rewrite/combat-action-budget-playtest.md; neither profile is approved or balanced.
